scope: Independent adversarial review of the R8 production delta against deployed R7, followed by independent execution of the final production-extraction capacity tests and existing lifetime harness. Production source and tests were read only; this reviewer authored only this report.

resolved_review_findings.finding: A new dynamic context with an unsupported preserved request could remain without a confirmed active interpolation count.
resolved_review_findings.resolution: Dispatch applies one legal fallback count when no active count exists, keeps the requested config unchanged, and subsequently retains the confirmed active count for requests above the initialized capacity. The extracted production guard tests this startup path.

resolved_review_findings.finding: A failed GetProperties call could discard a successfully patched advertised capability and leave a stale one-frame ceiling.
resolved_review_findings.resolution: Both swapchain creation paths initialize the supported ceiling from the successfully applied unlock limit before querying properties. Query success may supplement that capability; query failure does not remove it.

resolved_review_findings.finding: Legacy SDKs without SetNumInterpolatedFrames require restart for lower as well as higher multiplier changes.
resolved_review_findings.resolution: The menu distinguishes dynamic SDK support, displays restart information for changed legacy requests, preserves their requested counts, and avoids a redundant live FG toggle.

resolved_review_findings.finding: A request outside provider capability cannot be repaired by a restart alone.
resolved_review_findings.resolution: Unsupported requests receive a separate choose-a-supported-multiplier message instead of an inaccurate restart-only instruction.

verified_checks: The production pure policy selects capacity 3 interpolated frames (4X total) for explicit 2X/3X/4X requests with LowMemoryMode enabled, subject to actual support. Explicit 5X/6X, Auto and LowMemoryMode disabled reserve the full supported startup capacity. Legacy SDK startup behavior uses the selected count.

Both swapchain creation paths use the same policy. The process-fixed successful U4 allocation override is also used for C++ initialization parameters, preventing changes made after DLL loading from claiming a capacity the already patched SDK cannot honor.

The U4 patch immediate alone uses selected initialization capacity. U3/U5 preserve the configured advertised ceiling. Successful patch metadata distinguishes initial capacity from selectable support; failure does not publish applied metadata. Existing PE build and byte guards and transactional rollback remain.

Initialization readback records valid actual capacity within the supported ceiling, otherwise conservatively retains the requested capacity. Dynamic contexts reset the cached active count so a reused provider must apply its selected count again. Legacy contexts record their initialized active count directly.

Live 3X/4X changes call the existing SDK setter only within initialized and supported limits. Requests for 5X/6X in a 4X-capacity session remain saved selections and do not issue an unsupported setter call or replace the current active count. Warnings occur only when a rejected request changes.

The menu uses the selected config for its custom multiplier field and the confirmed active count for the current-state message. A pending 5X/6X choice is not overwritten by the lower active count. Save settings and restart are explicitly required for capacity growth.

Startup heap queries are labeled as SDK requirements rather than resident VRAM. They are not used as cleanup permission or a claim of measured allocation savings, and no query was added to the per-frame path.

No capacity change performs hot swapchain destruction/recreation, game-resource Release, eviction, forced cleanup, RAM spill, GPU flush or a new blocking fence wait. Existing R7 lifetime, submission admission, resource tracking, recovery and pacing paths remain structurally unchanged apart from initialization-capacity metadata resets.

Independent byte comparison to R7 found all 241 tracked shader paths, 12 FG input files and 11 selected lifetime/tracking/recovery/pacing files unchanged. This preserves their rendering code, not a measured guarantee of identical image quality on hardware.

The shipped Intel libxess_fg.dll SHA-256 and each of the five unlock patch RVAs independently matched the production expected bytes. The CPU patcher harness additionally checks low/full capacity, invalid override inputs, idempotence and rollback faults.

runtime_limitations: No Cyberpunk 2077, real Intel XeFG execution, RX 9070 XT measurement, Dogtown transition, long-session FPS recovery or visual comparison was performed by this reviewer.

Lower declared and patched maximum capacity is implemented and tested as a contract. Actual VRAM savings and performance improvement depend on the Intel runtime and driver and must be measured; SDK heap requirements are not physical residency or guaranteed savings.

R8 does not repair Cyberpunk RT Lighting Psycho engine allocations and does not establish a Psycho-preserving solution to the reported Dogtown slowdown. The user observed that Ultra restores performance, but this review does not reproduce or independently measure that observation.

A 4X-capacity session retains 5X/6X as selectable saved requests. Applying them requires Save settings and a game restart. Returning from a full-capacity session to 3X/4X does not free that capacity live; a subsequent restart selects the reduced capacity.

The binary unlock remains tied to the recognized pinned Intel runtime. Unknown builds or patch failures retain native capability rather than receiving unvalidated byte edits. This is not support for arbitrary future SDK versions.

CPU harnesses use explicit fake SDK, COM, driver and UI boundaries. They do not prove Windows ABI/hooking behavior, GPU scheduling, driver allocation behavior, steady-state overhead, device-loss recovery or memory-pressure recovery. Windows CI and final payload validation are separate build gates.

Pre-existing SetNumInterpolatedFrames failure retry behavior and inherited waits remain; this change does not eliminate every possible SDK/driver stall or retry. No arbitrary 2.5 GiB resource reclamation is attempted.
Source checks show unchanged algorithms in compared files. Real rendered output, FPS and latency are not guaranteed identical without an on-device A/B test.
